reason: Replacing Ta with its much lighter, chemically similar refractory congener Nb offers a substantial density reduction while plausibly retaining a BCC solid solution and high-temperature strengthening; the cited subtraction studies directly include HfMoNbTiZr and support Nb for elevated-temperature strength and ductility. In contrast, Ti-to-Sc substitution provides little atomic-mass benefit and Sc’s lower melting point and less compatible chemistry make phase stability and strength near 1000 °C substantially less credible.
